methods.label: LinearSearch v1
methods.description: Defensive copy of the input, then an index-based while-loop scan per query.

methods.label: LinearSearch v2
methods.description: No copy (the scan never mutates the input); direct for-loop iteration per query.

methods.label: BinarySearch v1
methods.description: sorted() copy, then recursive binary search with early exit on equality.

methods.label: BinarySearch v2
methods.description: sorted() copy, then iterative lower-bound binary search (no recursion).

methods.label: HashSet
methods.description: set() of the input, then one membership test per query.

definitions.prepare: One call of prepare(ids). linear v1: list copy; linear v2: no work (returns the input); binary: sorted() copy; hash: set() construction. Includes freeing the returned structure (each result is discarded inside the timed loop).
definitions.query: One complete batch of q queries, query(state, queries), on a state prepared freshly for each repeat outside the timed loop. Includes building the output list. Warm-cache, steady-state figure: within one measurement the same state and queries are reused calls_per_measurement times.
definitions.total: One prepare(ids) followed by one complete query batch, timed together (measured directly, not the sum of prepare and query). Every call builds a fresh structure and frees it, so total is generally not equal to prepare + query.
definitions.elapsed_s: Seconds per call: per prepare, per complete query batch, or per prepare+batch. Each measurement runs the call calls_per_measurement times in a loop and divides the elapsed time.perf_counter() time by that count. Per-query values (query batch / q) are derived, not measured.
definitions.repeats: A calibration run (which is also the warm-up) picks calls_per_measurement, plus a 25% margin, so one measurement lasts about >= min_measure_seconds; calls that already take that long run once. Actual duration of a measurement = elapsed_s * calls_per_measurement. Then `repeats` measurements per (dataset, method, version, segment); method order rotates each repeat. Report the median; all raw values are kept.
definitions.datasets: Grid n x q x scenario, except q=1 'mixed' (one query cannot be half present). Present queries are placed by first occurrence, evenly spread over the array (mean_first_hit_frac ~ 0.5), so linear-search hit costs are comparable across n and q. IDs are dense small ints (< 2^30): a best case for hashing and comparisons.
definitions.gc: Garbage collection is disabled inside timed loops (as timeit does); gc.collect() runs before each measurement.
definitions.excluded: Data generation, input validation, tests, correctness preflight checks, printing, memory tracing and dashboard rendering are outside timed regions.
definitions.memory: tracemalloc, in a separate process after timing. The input is built before tracing starts; each (dataset, method) gets a fresh tracing run. prepare_* is read after prepare(), total_* after the query batch, with state and output kept alive. Includes: the prepared structure, the output list, transient buffers (e.g. timsort's merge buffer, set resizing) in the peaks, and about 50-110 bytes of harness objects (see memory_baseline in run.json, not subtracted). Excludes: the input array and queries, and native allocations tracemalloc does not see. *_peak = highest traced bytes since tracing started; *_current = bytes still allocated then.
definitions.noop_call_s: Per-call overhead of the timing loop with the prepare/query wrapper (functools.partial around a no-op); noop_lambda_call_s is the same for the total segment's lambda. Not subtracted. Values within about 10x of these are dominated by overhead.
